summary: Bearish — Elevated Downside Risk remains unchanged before the scheduled 08:30 EST October PPI release. November 12 cash closes (Nasdaq -0.39%, SOX -0.54%, NVDA -4.34%, AMD +5.86%, AVGO +5.54%) remain the latest confirmed synchronized US equity evidence. Friday morning Nasdaq-100 futures around -0.11% to -0.13% and QQQ approximately flat are asynchronous pre-release indications, not a confirmed cash-session response. The most recent reported 10Y 5.130% and 2Y 4.861% imply +26.9 basis points, not +269bp. Open Watch advanced from 162 to 163 events, but the added item is not yet independently identified as a material three-day catalyst. Friday PPI actual, fresh VXN/VIX, breadth, cash SOX and live CME FedWatch are unverified.
bullish: Nasdaq closed -0.39% after opening -1.47%, showing substantial absorption of the initial Nvidia shock.
AMD +5.86% and AVGO +5.54% at Thursday's close indicate selective chip rotation rather than uniform sector capitulation.
Foxconn and Siemens data-center demand signals remain supportive of longer-run AI infrastructure spending; no attributable index response is established.

Applied Materials fiscal Q4 adjusted EPS $4.16 versus $4.06 expected and revenue $10.41B versus $10.3B; next-quarter guidance above estimates. Cisco reported adjusted EPS $1.40 versus $1.33 expected, revenue $18.5B versus $18.1B and raised outlook; positive AI networking demand evidence, not proof of Friday market response.
Friday Reuters oil report indicates Brent and WTI declined versus the previous reported session; if sustained, this could relieve inflation pressure, but this is not an observed US equity response.
New SMIC foundry commentary indicates persistent AI demand and supply tightness through 2027, a long-horizon demand/pricing signal rather than a confirmed immediate SOX catalyst.
Cerebras raised 2026 revenue guidance and announced Microsoft cloud deal, supporting AI-compute demand, without verified immediate QQQ/SOX impact.
A contemporaneous WSJ Asian-session report describes a tentative Asian chip-stock rebound; not confirmation of US semiconductor recovery.
Reuters Friday report indicates NVDA +1.8% premarket; no cash-session confirmation.
bearish: Nvidia closed -4.34% following the confirmed CEO transition, and SOX finished -0.54%; leadership and semiconductor benchmark remain vulnerable.
Higher oil and long yields reported earlier remain valuation risks, but current synchronized oil/yield measurements are missing.
Reuters reports at least a 25bp December Fed hike fully priced, with a 15% chance of a 50bp move; hotter PPI could worsen duration-sensitive equity pressure.
Applied Materials was reportedly nearly flat after hours despite its beat after falling 3.6% in regular trade; a strong report alone has not confirmed sector-wide risk appetite.

Reuters November 13 Asian-session coverage describes higher US yields and Nvidia-linked weakness across Asia, consistent with persistent duration and leadership risk; no matched Friday US QQQ/SOX confirmation.
SMIC says AI chip capacity may stay constrained through 2027, which may increase costs and delivery delays even as demand remains robust.
November 13 01:14 ET Investing.com report describes US equity futures turning lower, without verified matched index/semiconductor prices.
WSJ Friday Asian-session 10Y yield of 5.128% and 2Y 4.861% reinforce elevated discount-rate risk; data are not synchronized with US stock trading.
Reuters Friday report indicates MSFT -2.6% premarket amid prolonged service outages; sustained index impact not verified.

editorial.marketOverview: The Nasdaq/QQQ outlook remains downside-skewed before October PPI. Thursday's Nasdaq -0.39%, SOX -0.54% and NVDA -4.34% closing performance indicate leadership fragility, though AMD +5.86% and AVGO +5.54% demonstrate selective semiconductor demand. Friday premarket NVDA rebound and mixed futures do not establish a confirmed regular-session reversal. The last reported Treasury pair of 5.130% for 10Y and 4.861% for 2Y implies a +26.9bp curve spread; the high yield level remains a duration headwind.
editorial.whatChanged: Since the 06:38 EST assessment, secondary Friday premarket reporting showed NVDA +2.64% and MSFT -1.59% around 06:41 EST and Nasdaq-100 futures -0.13% at 05:42 EST. These are asynchronous observations and do not constitute a material bias change. The GitHub Open Watch feed increased from 162 to 163 events (updated 12:45 UTC), without verified independent three-day index impact. The October PPI release was still pending at the 08:20 EST assessment checkpoint.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Mixed premarket semiconductor action supports a selective rotation interpretation rather than broad capitulation or a confirmed recovery. PPI is a prospective catalyst, not an observed price response. A sustained QQQ/SOX recovery with easing rates and better breadth would challenge the bearish base case; isolated NVDA premarket gains cannot do so alone. High nominal yields and uncertain Fed repricing keep growth valuations exposed.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday November 13 depends on the 08:30 EST PPI surprise versus consensus and subsequent synchronized Treasury, QQQ, SOX and volatility reactions after the cash open. Monday November 16 should test whether that response persists. Tuesday November 17 adds import/export price data and potentially important AI earnings timing, which must be independently confirmed. Until actual PPI and price reaction are available, the base case remains volatile, downside-skewed consolidation rather than a confirmed breakdown.
editorial.bullCase: A benign PPI print followed by falling 2Y and 10Y yields, firm QQQ, improving SOX relative strength, NVDA stabilization, broadening participation and contained VXN/VIX could trigger a durable rebound. Thursday AMD and AVGO strength and constructive AMAT/Cisco demand reporting provide selective support, but Friday cash confirmation is required.
editorial.bearCase: A hotter PPI release, upward Treasury repricing and renewed Nvidia-led SOX underperformance would intensify downside risk. Weak Nasdaq breadth, rising VXN/VIX, renewed oil inflation pressure or Microsoft outage spillover would amplify pressure. None of these conditional developments should be recorded as already observed.
editorial.watchNext: Verify the official BLS October PPI actual and core details after 08:30 EST, then capture timestamp-matched 2Y/10Y, QQQ, Nasdaq, SOX, NVDA, breadth, VXN/VIX and Brent/WTI readings. Recheck CME FedWatch probabilities and inspect the newest Open Watch item for materiality. Keep forecast, asynchronous premarket indications and confirmed market reactions separate.
